lesson.title: Real-time remote biometric identification
lesson.summary: Identify the public-space law-enforcement ban and its three strictly limited objective branches.

prerequisites.reason: Real-time is a timing qualification of remote biometric identification.
The objectives apply to use for the defined law-enforcement purpose.
A permitted objective is one part of the statutory test rather than automatic permission.

blocks: **Real-time remote biometric identification** identifies people without their active involvement, typically at a distance, by comparison with a reference database, with capture, comparison and identification occurring without significant delay. Limited short delays cannot be used to evade the real-time definition.

A **publicly accessible space** is a physical place accessible to an undetermined number of people, regardless of ownership or access conditions. A privately owned station can qualify. Establish real-time identification, public accessibility and law-enforcement purpose together.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(41)–(44), Article 5(1)(h); Annex II

blocks: Article 5(1)(h) generally prohibits this use for law enforcement. An exception objective must be strictly necessary: targeted search for specific victims of abduction, human trafficking or sexual exploitation, or search for missing persons.

A second objective concerns preventing a specific, substantial and imminent threat to life or physical safety, or a genuine and present or genuine and foreseeable terrorist-attack threat. Generic crime prevention is not the wording of either objective.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(41)–(44), Article 5(1)(h); Annex II

blocks: The third objective concerns locating/identifying a suspect for investigation, prosecution or execution of a criminal penalty. The offence must be in **Annex II** and punishable in the Member State by a maximum custodial sentence or detention order of at least four years.

Annex II lists terrorism; human trafficking; child sexual exploitation/pornography; drug trafficking; weapons trafficking; murder/grievous bodily injury; organ/tissue trafficking; nuclear/radioactive-material trafficking; kidnapping/unlawful restraint/hostage-taking; International Criminal Court crimes; aircraft/ship hijacking; rape; environmental crime; organised/armed robbery; sabotage; participation in a criminal organisation involved in a listed offence. Verify the exact entry and national maximum penalty separately.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(41)–(44), Article 5(1)(h); Annex II

blocks: Fictional Northbridge station case: police seek a specified missing person. The objective can enter the exception assessment; it does not dispense with target limits, impact assessment, registration, authorisation and national law taught next.

Changed case: police scan everyone merely to discourage minor disorder. That general objective does not establish a listed exception. A post-event system or private-access system needs its own classification and other-law assessment; a different fact is not universal permission.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(41)–(44), Article 5(1)(h); Annex II

questions.prompt: A system compares faces to an identity database with only a short operational delay. What matters for the real-time definition?

options.reason: The definition includes limited short delays to prevent circumvention.

options.blocks: Any delay makes identification entirely unregulated
options.reason: Limited short delays do not automatically avoid the definition.

options.blocks: Only whether a vendor says the product is retrospective
options.reason: The actual operation determines the definition.

questions.prompt: A privately owned station admits an undetermined number of ticket holders. What public-space fact matters?

options.blocks: Every private owner makes the space legally inaccessible
options.reason: Ownership alone does not determine public accessibility.
The definition is not limited to outdoor places.

options.blocks: Public accessibility can exist despite ownership or conditions
options.reason: The definition concerns an undetermined number of persons, irrespective of those facts.

questions.prompt: For the suspect branch, an Annex II entry is established but the national maximum penalty is unknown. What remains unresolved?

options.blocks: Only the sentence police would prefer
options.reason: The statutory national maximum is the relevant threshold.

options.blocks: The national maximum of at least four years and other conditions
options.reason: The offence list and national penalty threshold are cumulative, with further safeguards.

options.blocks: Nothing; any listed offence automatically permits every use
options.reason: The penalty threshold and safeguards cannot be omitted.
